description:
🔴 ACTS FOR THE USER: call it only after the user has explicitly agreed to this exact action (what, where, when, who) — never on your own judgement.
For a business whose card shows an `order` action with method `connected`. Shopify: returns the shop’s
own checkout link with these items and quantities already in the cart (`status: unknown`, `mode: cart`)
— no customer data is needed or passed, the buyer gives their details and pays on Shopify, and nothing
exists on the shop until they do. Square: an order with a payment link (no customer data either).
WhatsApp: a message to the owner (customer phone or email). Returns `order_id`, `status`, `checkout_url`
— HAND THE CHECKOUT URL TO THE USER AS IT IS: that page takes the money, SuVerse holds no card and charges
nothing. Stock is checked live first on a platform that tracks it; «not in stock» is an `unavailable`
error and no order or link is given. Send an `idempotency_key` of your own and keep it for a retry: the
same key returns the same answer and the same link (`repeated: true`), never a second one. Lines name
offerings by their card id (and `variant_id` when the card lists several). `status`: unknown (a cart
link: payment is on the platform’s side) · created (the platform holds it) · pending_owner (WhatsApp) ·
confirmed · declined · failed. Get the user’s explicit yes before calling this.
Follow the server instructions «HOW TO USE THE SUVERSE CATALOG»: results are candidates, not proof; keep reading, quoting, requesting and ordering separate; nothing is sent to an owner, booked, ordered or paid without the user’s permission.

email.description: the buyer’s e-mail: the platform sends the checkout link and the receipt there (for a booking; NOT asked for an order on Shopify or Square, whose checkout asks the buyer)

name.description: the buyer’s name (required for a booking)

phone.description: the buyer’s telephone with country code

customer.description: only where the platform needs it (WhatsApp); omit for Shopify and Square

idempotency_key.description: your own key for this order; reuse it on a retry

note.description: a note to the business, in the user’s words (not passed on a Shopify cart link)

name: place_order
title: Place an order in the business’s own system; the buyer pays on the platform’s checkout page
